payroll.tax_declaration.description: Investment declaration rows — My Tax & Investments › Declarations (MyTaxAndInvestmentsPage › DeclarationsTab)

section.hint: The part of the income-tax law this saving comes under. It decides how much of it can lower your tax.

askMaya.question: Which income tax section should I choose when declaring an investment or expense, and what kinds of payments count under 80C, 80D, 80CCD(1B), HRA and LTA?

proof_reference.hint: A link or receipt number that shows you paid. HR checks it before the amount counts towards your tax saving.

verified_amount.hint: The amount HR accepted after checking your proof. It can be lower than what you declared if a receipt is missing or doesn’t cover it all.

payroll.tax_regime.description: Old vs new regime choice — My Tax & Investments › Regime (MyTaxAndInvestmentsPage › RegimeTab)

regime_code.hint: The set of rules used to work out your income tax. Under the old one your declared savings count; under the new one most don’t.

askMaya.question: What is the difference between the old and new income tax regime, and how do I decide which one to choose for this financial year?

payroll.bank_details.description: Salary bank account editor — My Salary › Bank details (MySalaryPage)

ifsc_code.hint: An 11-character code for your bank branch, such as SBIN0001234. It’s on your cheque book or passbook and in your bank’s app.

account_type.hint: Whether this is a savings or a current account. Salary almost always goes into a savings account.

askMaya.question: Should my salary be paid into a savings account or a current account, and what is the difference between them for salary payments?

attendance.regularization.description: Attendance correction request — My Attendance › Corrections › New request (RegularizationCard › RegularizationFormModal)

work_mode.hint: Where you worked that day. Leave it as recorded unless it was logged wrongly — it only changes if the correction is approved.

askMaya.question: When I request an attendance correction, what does the ‘Worked from’ option mean, and what is the difference between office, remote, field and hybrid work?

payroll.reimbursement_claim.description: Expense line in a reimbursement claim — My Reimbursements › New claim (MyReimbursementsPage › ClaimEditorDialog)

category_id.hint: The type of expense, such as travel or food. Your organisation sets these, and each can have its own limit and receipt rule.

askMaya.question: How do I choose the right expense category for a reimbursement claim, and when do I need to attach a receipt?

documents.upload.description: Add a document / upload a new version (shared DocumentUploadDialog — also used by HR and managers, hence the workspace gate)

document_number.hint: The number printed on the document itself, such as a PAN or passport number. It’s stored securely; only the last 4 characters are shown.

is_confidential.hint: Hides this document from your manager — only you and HR can see it. Once it’s confidential, it can’t be made visible again.

askMaya.question: What happens when I mark a document as confidential, who can still see it, and can I change it back later?

leaves.apply.description: Apply for leave drawer (LeaveDashboard › ApplyLeaveDrawer; also mounted under the HR and manager prefixes). Holds the form field plus the balance strip: `pending_hold` is summed client-side from requests still pending, and “Effective” = current_balance − pending_hold (explained in the same hint).

leave_type_id.hint: The kind of leave you’re taking, such as sick or casual. Each has its own balance and rules; days beyond your balance may be unpaid.

askMaya.question: What is the difference between leave types such as casual, sick and earned leave, and what happens if I apply for more days than my leave balance?

pending_hold.hint: Days in your requests still waiting for approval. They’re set aside, so “Effective” is what you can still apply for.

askMaya.question: What does pending hold mean on my leave balance, and when are held days given back or taken from my balance?

attendance.summary.description: Month headline figures from /attendance/graph-data › summary (EmployeeDashboard › My month)

punctuality_percentage.hint: Of the days you clocked in this month, the share you arrived on time. Arriving within your grace period still counts as on time.

askMaya.question: How is on-time arrival worked out in attendance, and what is the grace period for clocking in late?

attendance.daily_log.description: Per-day attendance record (graph-data › daily, /attendance/history). Shown as the “Effective” column on the Dashboard’s Recent days and on My Attendance.

effective_hours.hint: Time on the clock minus your breaks. It decides whether the day counts as a full day, a half day or absent.

askMaya.question: What are effective working hours, how are breaks taken out of them, and how many hours do I need for a full day or a half day?

attendance.anomalies.description: My Flags list (/attendance/anomalies/mine) › “Flag” column — `type`, falling back to `anomaly_type`

type.hint: Your manager or HR reviews each flag and marks it sorted out. If one looks wrong, talk to them — you don’t need to raise it anywhere else.

askMaya.question: What does it mean when my attendance is flagged, for example outside the office location or a break over the limit, and what should I do about it?

overtime_minutes.hint: Time worked beyond the hours your policy needs for a full day — not beyond your shift. It counts once approved, if your policy needs approval.

askMaya.question: How is overtime calculated from my attendance, does it need my manager’s approval, and what do I get for approved overtime?

leaves.balances.description: Leave balance cards (/leaves/my-balances) — one ⓘ on the “Leave Balances” heading covers “given so far” (`total_accrued`) on every card

total_accrued.hint: “Given so far” is the leave added this year — all at once or month by month, depending on your policy. “Days left” is what you can still take.

askMaya.question: How is leave added to my balance during the year, and what happens to unused leave at the end of the year?

unpaid_days.hint: Days beyond your leave balance are taken without pay, so that month’s salary is lower. The split is worked out when you submit.

askMaya.question: What is leave without pay (LWP), when does leave become unpaid, and how does it reduce my salary?

payroll.my_salary.description: My Salary headline (/payroll/me/salary-structure). `take_home_monthly` is derived by statutoryTotals() — gross minus statutory and salary deductions.

annual_ctc.hint: The company’s total yearly cost for you, not what you’re paid. Deductions such as PF and tax come off first, so what reaches your bank is lower.

askMaya.question: What is CTC (cost to company), and why is my take-home pay lower than my CTC?

take_home_monthly.hint: An estimate from your salary structure. What actually reaches your bank each month can change with unpaid leave, attendance and tax.

askMaya.question: Why can the salary that reaches my bank differ from month to month, and what affects my take-home pay?

payroll.statutory.description: Statutory deduction lines (StatutoryBreakdown AmountTable). Wired generically by `line.key` (pf, esi, pt, tds, pf_employer, esi_employer, edli, pf_admin) — only the keys listed here show an ⓘ.

pf.hint: Part of your pay saved into your provident fund account, with the company adding its own share. It’s your money, for retirement.

askMaya.question: What is the provident fund (EPF) deduction from salary, how much is deducted, and how can I withdraw or check my PF balance?

pt.hint: A small tax charged by some states on salaried people. Whether it applies, and how much, depends on the state you work in.

askMaya.question: What is professional tax, how is it calculated, and why does it differ between states?

payable_days.hint: The days you’re paid for this month. Unpaid leave and unrecorded absences bring it below the number of days in the month.

askMaya.question: What are paid days on a payslip, and why can they be fewer than the days in the month?

remaining_tds.hint: Income tax for the year that hasn’t been taken from your pay yet. It’s spread over the months left, so it changes if your pay or declarations do.

askMaya.question: How is income tax (TDS) deducted from my salary each month, and why does the monthly amount change during the year?

previous_employer.hint: Pay and tax from a job you left earlier this financial year. It’s added in so your tax for the whole year is worked out correctly.

askMaya.question: Why does income from my previous employer this year affect my tax, and what is Form 12B?

standard_deduction.hint: A fixed amount taken off your salary before tax is worked out. It’s given automatically — you don’t need to declare or prove anything.

askMaya.question: What is the standard deduction on salary income, and how does it reduce my income tax?

form16.hint: Your yearly tax certificate from the company. Part A lists the tax deposited for you; Part B shows how it was worked out. You use it to file your return.

askMaya.question: What is Form 16, what is the difference between Part A and Part B, and how do I use it to file my income tax return?

payroll.loans.description: Loan detail dialog (/payroll/me/loans) › “How interest is worked out” (`interest_method`)

interest_method.hint: Flat charges interest on the full amount for the whole loan. “On what’s still owed” charges it only on the unpaid part, so it costs you less.

askMaya.question: What is the difference between flat interest and reducing balance interest on a salary loan?

divisor_days.hint: Your monthly pay is divided by this many days to get one day’s rate. The number is set by your company’s policy.

askMaya.question: How is the amount for leave encashment calculated, and what does dividing the month by a number of days mean?

payroll.reimbursement_limits.description: My Claims & Benefits › Limits tab (/payroll/me/reimbursements/categories) › “Period limit” column

period_limit.hint: The most you can claim in this category in each period, such as a month. It starts again each period; “Per claim” caps a single claim.

askMaya.question: How do reimbursement limits work, what is the difference between a per-claim limit and a period limit, and when do they reset?

status.hint: In review: HR hasn’t checked it yet. Action required: HR sent it back — upload it again. Not finished: the upload didn’t complete.

askMaya.question: What do the document statuses in review, action required, not finished and expiring soon mean, and what do I need to do for each?

documents.company_documents.description: My Company Documents › status filter (`compliance_state`: pending, overdue, completed, waived)

compliance_state.hint: Needs you: read, acknowledge or sign it. Overdue: its due date has passed. Excused: HR decided you don’t need to act on it.

askMaya.question: What do I need to do with documents issued to me by the company, and what do needs you, overdue and excused mean?

payroll.adjustment_proposal.description: Salary Adjustments — the manager proposes, HR creates directly. Same fields, same dialog shape (ManagerAdjustmentsPage / PayrollAdjustmentsPage).

adjustment_type.hint: Add a one-off amount to their pay, or take one off, in the month you choose. Their salary structure doesn’t change.

askMaya.question: What is a one-off salary adjustment, and how is an extra earning or a deduction for one month different from a salary revision?

component_name.hint: The name shown for this line on their payslip, such as Spot Award. Leave it blank to use a standard name.

period_month.hint: The pay month this is added to or taken from. It has to be a month whose payroll isn’t approved or paid yet.

payroll.bonus_proposal.description: A one-off bonus — the manager proposes, HR creates directly (ManagerAdjustmentsPage / PayrollAdjustmentsPage).

bonus_type.hint: Flat ₹ gives everyone the same amount. The % options work it out from each person’s basic or gross pay, so Value is then a percentage.

askMaya.question: What is the difference between basic pay and gross pay, and how is a bonus worked out as a percentage of each?

payroll.loan_recommendation.description: A loan or salary advance — the manager recommends, HR creates it and sets the schedule (ManagerAdjustmentsPage / PayrollLoansPage).

loan_type.hint: A salary advance is pay given early; a company loan is money the company lends. Both are paid back in monthly instalments from salary.

askMaya.question: What is the difference between a salary advance and a company loan, and how is each paid back from salary?

tenure_months.hint: The number of months it’s paid back over. One instalment is taken from their pay each month.

start_period_month.hint: The pay month the first instalment is taken from their salary. The rest follow month by month.

payroll.salary_revision.description: A new salary — the manager proposes, HR assigns it directly (TeamSalaryPage / EmployeeSalaryStructuresPage).

annual_ctc.hint: The company’s total yearly cost for them, not what they’re paid. PF, tax and other deductions come off first, so take-home is lower.

askMaya.question: What is included in CTC (cost to company), and how does a change in CTC affect monthly take-home pay?

revision_type.hint: Why the pay is changing: a regular raise, a promotion, fixing an earlier mistake, or a restructure of how the pay is split. It’s kept on record.

askMaya.question: What is the difference between a salary increment, a promotion, a correction and a restructure when revising someone’s salary?

effective_from.hint: The date the new pay starts. It must be after the current salary’s start. If it falls in a month already paid, the difference comes in a later payroll.

payroll.encashment_proposal.description: Manager asks HR to pay a report for earned leave days — Encashments › Cash out earned leave.

period_month.hint: The pay month the cash-out is added to once HR approves it. Pick a month whose payroll isn’t approved or paid yet.

payroll.claim_review.description: Item-by-item approval of a reimbursement claim — ClaimDecisionDialog, shared by the manager (step 1) and HR (final) reviews.

category_limits.hint: How much of each expense type’s limit is left for this person after what you approve. Going over is refused, so lower the amount to fit.

askMaya.question: How do expense category limits work for reimbursement claims, and what happens when an approved amount would go over the limit?

documents.recommendation.description: Manager’s verify/reject recommendation on a report’s document — RecommendDialog in DocumentDetailDialog (manager plane only).

recommendation.hint: Normally HR makes the final call. If your organisation gives managers direct authority, your recommendation decides it straight away.

askMaya.question: What does a manager’s recommendation to verify or reject an employee’s document mean, and who makes the final decision?

documents.request.description: Asking one person for one kind of document — RequestDocumentDialog, shared by HR (#80) and managers (#93).

due_on.hint: Leave it blank to use your organisation’s standard time limit. Reminder emails go out automatically until it’s provided.

documents.upload_for_report.description: DocumentUploadDialog when someone uploads for another person — the manager’s Upload for a report, HR’s request and profile uploads. Chosen by the host’s helpSurface prop.

document_number.hint: The number printed on the document itself, such as a PAN or passport number. It’s stored securely; only the last 4 characters are shown.

is_confidential.hint: Only HR and the employee can see it — managers can’t, even one who uploaded it. Once it’s confidential, it can’t be made visible again.

askMaya.question: What happens when a document is marked confidential, who can still see it, and can it be made visible again later?

attendance.team.description: Team attendance figures a manager reads — Dashboard › Team today, Live Attendance, Attendance History, and the Effective/Overtime columns of the approval queues (shared with the HR Inbox). late_early is derived from late_minutes + early_exit_minutes.

final_absent_count.hint: Everyone not present or on leave today — including people who haven’t clocked in yet, so it drops as the day goes on.

askMaya.question: How is an employee marked present, late, absent or half day in attendance, and when does a missing punch count as absent?

late_minutes.hint: How late they clocked in against their shift. Arriving within the grace period isn’t late, and a late day still counts as present.

effective_hours.hint: Time on the clock minus breaks. It decides whether the day counts as a full day, a half day or absent.

askMaya.question: What are effective working hours in attendance, how are breaks taken out, and how many hours make a full day or a half day?

late_early.hint: How late they arrived and how early they left, against their shift. Arriving within the grace period isn’t counted as late.

overtime_minutes.hint: Time worked beyond the hours the policy needs for a full day — not beyond the shift. Once approved, it counts towards that period’s payroll.

askMaya.question: How is overtime calculated from attendance, when does it need a manager’s approval, and how is approved overtime paid?

attendance.approval_queue.description: Columns of the shared attendance approval queue (AttendanceApprovalQueue) — manager request pages, the manager Inbox and the HR Inbox/HR queues.

work_mode.hint: Where they worked: first as recorded, then what they’re asking to change it to. It only changes if the correction is approved.

days_earned.hint: Half or a full day, depending on the hours worked on the holiday or weekly off. Once approved it’s added to their leave and expires if unused.

askMaya.question: How is comp-off earned for working on a holiday or weekly off, how many days does it give, and when does it expire?

leaves.approval.description: Leave approvals — the manager's LeaveRequestCard (Leave Requests, Inbox) and HR's own leave request dialog. paid_split is the Paid/Unpaid split; balance_after is the balance once the request is approved, so it is wired only on the approval case, never on a cancellation where the same tile means the opposite.

paid_split.hint: Paid days come out of their leave balance. Days beyond it are unpaid (LWP), so that month’s salary is lower. The split is set when they apply.

askMaya.question: What is leave without pay (LWP), when does leave become unpaid, and how does it reduce an employee’s salary?

balance_after.hint: Their balance once you approve. A policy may allow a few extra days below zero, paid back from leave added later; beyond that, approval is refused.

askMaya.question: Can a leave balance go below zero, how are the extra days paid back, and what happens when a request needs more days than allowed?

payroll.team_salary.description: Team pay aggregates — Employee Salaries › Total CTC / Average CTC tiles (team_ctc_total, team_ctc_average).

team_ctc_total.hint: The yearly cost of everyone who reports to you, added up — not what they’re paid. It shows even when individual pay is hidden.

askMaya.question: What is CTC (cost to company), and what is the difference between CTC, gross pay and take-home pay?

payroll.pay_days.description: Loss-of-pay days wherever they appear for someone else’s pay — manager Payslips, the team run summary and Payroll Reports (shared with HR).

lop_days.hint: Loss of pay: days in the month the person isn’t paid for, such as unpaid leave or unrecorded absences. They lower that month’s pay.

askMaya.question: What are loss of pay (LOP) days, what causes them, and how are they deducted from salary?

payroll.reports.description: PayrollReportsView column headers, wired by column key — shared by HR Payroll Reports and the manager’s team reports. The config chooses which columns get help.

ctc_cost.hint: Gross pay plus what the company pays on top, such as its PF and ESI share. It’s the full cost of employing them.

askMaya.question: What does cost to company include beyond gross salary, and what are employer PF and ESI contributions?

total_employer_contributions.hint: PF, ESI and related charges the company pays on top of salary. They’re never deducted from the employee’s pay.

askMaya.question: What are employer contributions to PF and ESI, how are they calculated, and why are they not deducted from the employee’s salary?

payroll.salary_structure.description: SalaryStructurePanel component table — Team › member › Salary and Employee Salaries history for managers; an employee’s Salary tab for HR. calculation_basis is the “How it’s worked out” column (calculation_type + value).

calculation_basis.hint: A fixed amount, or a percentage of CTC, basic or gross pay. “Auto (remainder)” takes whatever is left so the parts add up to the CTC.

askMaya.question: How are salary components calculated — as a fixed amount, a percentage of basic or CTC, or a balancing amount — and why is one part the remainder?

documents.team_compliance.description: Manager Document Compliance — the “Where they’re at” column (compliance_state) for a report’s company documents.

compliance_state.hint: Waiting: still to read, acknowledge or sign. Overdue: the due date has passed. Excused: HR let them off. You can remind them; only they can act.

askMaya.question: What do the document compliance states waiting, overdue and excused mean, and who can acknowledge or sign a company document?

documents.proposals.description: Manager Document Proposals — the outcome tiles marked “(this page)”, counted from the rows loaded on the current page.

outcome_counts.hint: These count only the proposals loaded on this page, not all of them. Move through the pages to see the rest.

documents.letter_bulk.description: HR — Send a letter to many people (BulkIssueLettersDialog, #143). The subject list is the one field with a rule that isn't visible on screen.

subject_user_ids.hint: A batch goes out whole or not at all: if one person can’t be sent this letter, nobody is, and you’re told who to take out.

askMaya.question: When I send one letter to many people at once, what happens if some of them can’t be sent it, and does anyone ever get two copies?

documents.letter_settings.description: HR — Document Settings, the letters-to-many card (#91–#94) and the Phase 5 limits (#95 retention, #96 the hourly batch allowance). Auto-issue on exit and retention both act with nobody watching.

letter_auto_issue_on_exit.hint: Letters listed here are issued to a leaver on their last working day, with nobody reviewing them first. Leave it empty and nothing is automatic.

askMaya.question: What does issuing letters automatically when someone leaves actually do, and which kinds of letter can never be issued that way?

letter_bulk_rate_per_hour.hint: Past this many batches in an hour, the next person to send one is asked to wait. It guards against the same batch being sent over and over.

letter_record_retention_days.hint: How long a deleted letter is kept before it is destroyed for good. Lowering it destroys older ones on the next overnight run, and nothing undoes that.

askMaya.question: How long do we have to keep employment letters after deleting them, and which ones can never be destroyed even when the retention period has passed?

payroll.component_setup.description: HR — Setup › Salary Components, the create/edit component dialog. The behavioural flags decide how every structure built from this component behaves; none of them is explained on screen.

calculation_type.hint: How the amount is worked out: a fixed sum, a share of basic, gross or CTC, or the balancing line that absorbs whatever the others leave over.

askMaya.question: In a salary structure, what do flat amount, percentage of basic, percentage of gross, percentage of CTC and a balancing component mean, and when is each one used?

is_basic.hint: Marks this as the basic pay the rest builds on — PF and every percentage-of-basic component are worked out from it. Only one component can be it.

askMaya.question: Why does basic salary matter in an Indian salary structure, and which deductions and allowances are calculated as a percentage of basic?

is_part_of_ctc.hint: Counts this inside the CTC on the employee’s offer. Switch it off and it is paid on top, so the yearly cost runs above the figure they were given.

askMaya.question: What does CTC include, and how is it different from gross salary and from what reaches the bank?

pf_applicable.hint: Adds this component to the wages PF is worked out on, so switching it on raises both the employee’s deduction and the employer’s share.

askMaya.question: Which salary components count towards PF wages, and how are the employee and employer PF contributions worked out?

payroll.statutory_config.description: HR — Setup › Tax & Legal Deductions (TaxConfigurationsPage), the PF / ESI / PT / TDS rate cards. Rendered from the FIELD_GROUPS descriptors, so each help is attached to the descriptor, not the markup. Hints carry no rates or limits — those change with the law.

pf_wage_ceiling.hint: The most of a month’s wages PF is worked out on. It only bites when the setting below is on; otherwise PF follows the full PF wage.

askMaya.question: What is the PF wage ceiling, and what changes for an employee when the employer restricts PF to the ceiling instead of actual wages?

pf_restrict_to_ceiling.hint: On, PF stops at the ceiling for everyone earning above it. Off, it follows their full PF wage — more saved for them, more cost for the company.

esi_wage_threshold.hint: Earn up to this in a month and ESI is deducted. Cross it and cover runs to the end of the contribution period before it stops, not straight away.

askMaya.question: Who is covered by ESI, and what happens when an employee’s salary rises above the ESI limit part-way through the year?

tds_no_pan_rate.hint: The higher rate income tax is cut at while someone has no PAN on file. Adding their PAN puts them back on the normal slab from the next payroll.

askMaya.question: Why is income tax deducted at a higher rate when an employee has not given their PAN, and what happens once the PAN is provided?

payroll.settings.description: HR — Setup › Payroll Settings. Almost every switch on this screen already carries its own explanation line, so only the unpaid-day divisor is helped here.

lop_basis.hint: Sets what one unpaid day costs: the month’s pay split over 30 days, over that month’s days, or over its working days. Working days make a day dearest.

askMaya.question: How is one day’s pay worked out when an employee has unpaid days in a month, and why do companies divide the monthly salary differently?

leaves.policy_setup.description: HR — Setup › Leave Policies, the leave-quota dialog inside a policy. The quota, accrual and probation fields already carry their own lines on screen; these three do not say what happens afterwards.

max_carry_forward.hint: The most unused days that move into next year. Anything above it is lost when the year closes, unless the leave is paid out instead.

askMaya.question: What does carrying leave forward to the next year mean, and what usually happens to unused days above the limit?

max_negative_balance.hint: How far past zero someone may go on this leave. Days taken below zero come back out of a later quota, or off their final pay if they leave first.

notice_period_max_days.hint: What happens to this leave once somebody has resigned — no limit, none allowed at all, or a set number of days across the whole notice period.

attendance.policy_setup.description: HR — Setup › Attendance Policies, the policy dialog. Nearly every field there carries its own range line, so only the two that decide whether a day is paid are helped.

half_day_min_hours.hint: Work less than this on a working day and it counts as absent rather than a half day, so the day is unpaid unless leave or a correction covers it.

askMaya.question: How do effective working hours decide whether a day counts as a full day, a half day or absent, and what happens to pay for a half day?

missing_punch_action.hint: What happens to a day somebody never clocked out of: hold it for review, treat it as a half day, or mark it absent — which makes it unpaid.

attendance.comp_off_policy.description: HR — Setup › Comp-off Policies. The hours, multiplier, priority and cap fields all carry their own lines; expiry is the one rule that quietly takes earned time off away.

validity_days.hint: How long a credited day stays usable. Once it passes, the day is gone — it is not paid out — so a short window can waste time people have already worked.

payroll.structure_template.description: HR — Setup › Structure Templates: the template dialog and its Add Component row. Both fields are named after the engine, not after what they do.

definition_mode.hint: Start from a yearly CTC and split it into components, or add components up to whatever total they reach. CTC-driven needs a balancing component.

askMaya.question: What is the difference between building a salary structure from a total CTC downwards and building it up from individual components?

calculation_type.hint: How this line is worked out inside the template: a fixed sum, a share of basic, gross or CTC, or the balancing line that takes up whatever is left.

payroll.bonus_rule.description: HR — Setup › Bonus Rules, the rule dialog. The percentage note already explains the base it uses; this covers the choice above it.

bonus_type.hint: Whether everyone who qualifies gets the same amount, or a share of their own salary. It decides what the field beside it means.

payroll.benefit_plan.description: HR — Setup › Benefit Plans, the Advanced block of the plan dialog. Which component the money is taken through decides how it shows on the payslip.

employee_component_id.hint: The deduction line the employee’s share is charged through, so it is what they see on their payslip. Left empty, payroll picks a component itself.

payroll.run_item.description: HR — Payroll Runs › a run › one employee's record inspector (PayrollRunDetailPage). Derived figures the engine produced; the run's own status already carries a hint line, so it gets none.

ctc_cost.hint: What this person costs the company this month — their pay plus the employer’s share of PF, ESI and benefits. It is not what they receive.

askMaya.question: What is the difference between cost to company, gross pay and what reaches an employee’s bank account?

lop_divisor.hint: The number of days this month’s pay was split over to price one unpaid day. It follows the unpaid-day rule set in Payroll Settings.

carry_forward_out.hint: A deduction there wasn’t enough pay left to take this month. It is carried over and taken from a later payroll instead of being written off.

pf_wage.hint: The part of this month’s pay PF was worked out on — only the components marked PF-applicable, capped at the ceiling if that setting is on.

askMaya.question: Which parts of a salary count as PF wages, and why is PF often worked out on less than the gross salary?

payroll.arrears.description: HR — Payroll › Pay Differences (PayrollArrearsPage, API #203–#205). The difference column is the whole screen; its mechanism is in the file header and nowhere on screen.

net_delta.hint: What the month would work out to now, less what was already paid. Paying it adds the difference to the next open month; the old payslip is never rewritten.

askMaya.question: What is backdated pay in payroll, and why is it paid in a later month instead of correcting the original payslip?

payroll.bank_verification.description: HR — Payroll › Bank Verification. What verifying an account actually certifies. The self-verify guard in verifyAction() already explains itself when it bites; this covers the column for everyone else.

is_verified.hint: Verified means a second person checked the details against a passbook or cheque. It is not a check with the bank, and nobody may clear their own account.

payroll.tax_verification.description: HR — Tax › Tax Declarations, the verification dialog. The employee-facing payroll.tax_declaration entries are written to the employee about their own proof, so they must not be reused here (§2 voice rule).

verified_amount.hint: The amount you accept is what lowers their tax for the rest of the year. Accept less than they declared and more income tax comes out of their next payslips.

askMaya.question: How does verifying an investment declaration change the income tax deducted from an employee’s salary for the rest of the financial year?

organization.invite.description: HR — People › Invites, the invite dialog (InviteMemberModal). The role decides what the person can see of everyone else, and nothing on the form says so.

role.hint: What they will see: an employee only their own records, a manager their team’s as well, and an HR admin the whole organisation — pay included.

payroll.year_end.description: HR — Tax › Year-End & Form 16, the employee dialog. payroll.form16 is written to the employee about their own certificate, so it is not reused here (§2 voice rule). The hint asserts only what the same screen shows: provisional goes with a year that is still open.

is_provisional.hint: Provisional means this was worked out from a year that is still open, so the figures can change until the year is closed for that employee.

statutory_summary.hint: What was deducted for PF, ESI, professional tax and TDS each month, to prepare the payments. It isn’t a return you can upload for filing.

askMaya.question: What is a statutory challan, and how is it different from a PF ECR, an ESI return and a 24Q TDS return?

payroll.adjustment_admin.description: HR — Payroll › Salary Adjustments, the fields the manager's proposal form does not have. The type, component and pay month come from payroll.adjustment_proposal, which HR now shares (§2).

category.hint: Groups this line for reports and payslips. It does not change the amount or the tax — pick the one that describes why the money is moving.

payroll.encashment_admin.description: HR — Payroll › Leave Payouts, the pay-out dialog. payroll.encashment_proposal says “once HR approves it”, which is wrong when HR is the one filling the form, so the month gets its own entry here (§2 voice rule).

period_month.hint: The pay month the payout lands in. It has to be a month whose payroll is not approved or paid yet, or there is nothing left to add it to.

payroll.structure_assign.description: HR — Payroll › Employee Salaries, the assign/revise dialog. The CTC, effective date and revision type come from payroll.salary_revision, which HR now shares; the template picker is HR-only.

template_id.hint: The template decides how the yearly CTC is split into basic, allowances and deductions. Changing it later rebuilds the whole structure.

askMaya.question: What is a salary structure template, and how does it decide the split between basic pay, allowances and deductions?

payroll.tax_regime_config.description: HR — Setup › Tax & Legal Deductions › Income-Tax Regimes, the regime cards. Pure tax vocabulary with nothing on screen to explain it. No figures in the hints — every one of these changes with the finance act.

standard_deduction.hint: A flat amount taken off salary before tax is worked out. Everyone on this regime gets it — nobody has to declare anything to earn it.

askMaya.question: What is the standard deduction on salary income, and does an employee have to declare anything to claim it?

rebate_87a_income_limit.hint: Total income up to this figure pays no income tax at all, because the rebate cancels what would otherwise be due.

askMaya.question: What is the section 87A rebate, and how does it mean some salaried employees pay no income tax at all?

allows_chapter_via.hint: Whether savings an employee declares — 80C, 80D and the rest — can lower their tax on this regime. Switched off, declaring changes nothing.

askMaya.question: Which tax deductions can be claimed under the old regime but not the new one, and what does Chapter VI-A cover?

payroll.pt_slabs.description: HR — Setup › Tax & Legal Deductions › Professional Tax Slabs, the per-state slab tables. PT is the one deduction the organisation does not set the rate for.

amount.hint: Professional tax is charged by the state, not by this organisation. What comes off depends on where the employee works and what they earn.

askMaya.question: What is professional tax, which states charge it, and how is the monthly amount decided for a salaried employee?

documents.verification.description: HR — Documents We Collect › Verification Queue. The manager's recommendation is advice; only HR's decision moves the document out of the queue.

recommendation.hint: What the employee’s manager advised. It is only advice — the document stays in this queue until you verify or reject it yourself.

documents.letter_queue_health.description: HR — Document Automation, the letter render queue readout (#151). Every figure is derived, and the failure rate has a real null.

queued.hint: Letters asked for but not yet produced. They are made in the background, so a few waiting is normal right after a busy moment.

oldest_queued_age_seconds.hint: How long the letter at the front of the queue has been waiting. A long wait here, not a big number, is what means something is stuck.

failure_rate.hint: The share of letters that finished but didn’t come out. It reads N/A when nothing finished — that is no news, not a clean result.

payroll.payslip_queue_health.description: HR — Payroll Automation, the payslip render queue readout (#221). The payroll twin of documents.letter_queue_health; same figures, same wording.

queued.hint: Payslips asked for but not yet produced. They are made in the background, so a few waiting is normal right after a busy moment.

oldest_queued_age_seconds.hint: How long the payslip at the front of the queue has been waiting. A long wait here, not a big number, is what means something is stuck.

failure_rate.hint: The share of payslips that finished but didn’t come out. It reads N/A when nothing finished — that is no news, not a clean result.

leaves.assign_policy.description: HR — Assign a leave policy (AssignLeavePolicyDialog), from the employee profile's Leave tab and from the org-wide Leave Requests page. The one destructive action in Leave: it replaces every rule the person has.

template_id.hint: Sets how many days of each kind of leave this person gets. It replaces any rules they already have, and their days are worked out from the day they joined.

askMaya.question: When someone is given a leave policy part-way through the year, how are their leave days worked out, and what happens to days they had already been given?

organization.org_chart.description: Org Chart (OrgChartPage) — stat tiles, and the person dialog (OrgPersonDialog). depth, biggest_team, team_size and level are derived in orgChartMeta.js; reporting_to_id is the hierarchy node key.

depth.hint: How many layers there are from the top of the organisation down to the people furthest from it.

biggest_team.hint: The most people who report directly to one person. People further down their line aren’t counted here.

reporting_to_id.hint: Who this person reports to, all the way up. The manager directly above them is the one who reviews their leave and attendance requests.

askMaya.question: What is a reporting line in a company, and how does the person I report to affect who reviews my leave and attendance requests?

team_size.hint: Everyone below this person on the chart: the people who report to them, the people who report to those people, and so on.

level.hint: How far down the chart this person sits. Level 1 is the top of the organisation; each step down adds one.

organization.company_profile.description: Company Profile (CompanyProfilePage) — the People headline and the HR-only Tax & legal registration card. Keys are GET /organizations/details response keys.

total_active_members.hint: People who have joined and can sign in today. Invitations not yet accepted and people who have left aren’t counted.

gst_number.hint: The company’s GST registration number. Suppliers, customers and tax filings use it to identify the business.

askMaya.question: What is a GSTIN, what does each part of the 15-character number mean, and where does a company need to use it?

company_pan_number.hint: The company’s own income-tax number — not any employee’s PAN. It appears on the Form 16 given to employees.

askMaya.question: What is a company PAN, how is it different from a TAN, and where does it appear in salary tax documents like Form 16?

documents.catalog.description: Document Types › Catalog (DocumentTypesPage › CatalogTab) — the ready-made PDF letter filter. letter_template is a concept key: a catalog row paired with a #135 letter template (catalogLetterMeta.js).

letter_template.hint: Types HR Clouds can write for you as a branded PDF. Activate the type here, then switch its letter on under Letter Templates.

organization.company_profile_edit.description: Edit company details (EditCompanyProfileDialog, HR only) — keys are PATCH /organizations/profile body keys. Ordinary fields (industry, address, phone, description) carry no hint.

org_name.hint: Renames the organisation everywhere, not just on this page — sign-in, invitation emails and documents all use it.

size.hint: A band, not an exact count — the headcount on this page is counted from the people who have joined.

gst_number.hint: The company’s GST registration number. Only HR can see or change it.

askMaya.question: What is a GSTIN, what does each part of the 15-character number mean, and where does a company need to use it?

company_pan_number.hint: The company’s own income-tax number — not any employee’s PAN. It appears on the Form 16 given to employees.

askMaya.question: What is a company PAN, how is it different from a TAN, and where does it appear in salary tax documents like Form 16?

payroll.settlement.description: Final settlement record inspector (PayrollExitsPage › SettlementPanel) — the #224 statement download. Keys name the concept, as the statement has no response key of its own.

settlement_statement.hint: Provisional until the final pay goes out in a payroll run: payouts and recoveries only. The final one adds the last month’s pay and what was paid.

askMaya.question: What goes into a full and final settlement, and why can a provisional statement differ from the final one?

payroll.run_payslips.description: Payslips & delivery panel on a payroll run (RunPayslipsPanel) — the two bank advice files (#181 CSV, #223 PDF).

bank_advice.hint: Upload the CSV to your bank to pay everyone. The PDF is a printable copy to sign and keep on file — account numbers are hidden, so a bank can’t use it.
